lines: Particle-conserving sampling stays in the selected sector.
The neural output itself is unconstrained outside that sector.
slides.footer: All overlaps and VMC expectations use canonical-sector normalization; no full-Fock-space leakage curve is claimed.

slides.footer: Tiny ED also has analytic-limit and independent ladder-operator checks. Finite-χ and finite-size effects are separate from Monte Carlo SEM; modest length changes do not establish bulk convergence.

slides.title: Compare: ED-supervised fitting
slides.subtitle: 3×3 cylinder; Adam + normalized log-MSE; width 32; original Jastrow
slides.footer: Unsquared overlap criterion ≥0.99 qualifies neural candidates. Basic Jastrow remains a physical baseline even when its cylinder overlap is lower; no universality is assumed.

slides.title: Supervised objective
lines: Log-MSE is primary; infidelity refinement is a separate diagnostic.
slides.footer: The ED targets are strictly positive in these sectors; no 3×3-cylinder amplitudes are clamped by the chosen 10⁻¹² floor.

slides.title: Capacity and loss checks
slides.footer: 3×3 cylinder. FC/RBM enlarged from qualified states, with independent raw-ED checks. Basic Jastrow is a physical baseline; no further adaptation or common neural accuracy requirement.

slides.title: Variational Monte Carlo
lines: Equilibrate fresh walkers before updates; assess frozen checkpoints.
slides.footer: Retained configurations are correlated. Proposal spacing, burn-in, independent evaluation chains and time-block statistics are recorded.

slides.title: Stochastic reconfiguration
lines: VMC: SR direction applied with native SGD; no Adam on top.
slides.footer: 2D uses centered, sample-normalized covariance. The original 1D CPU code used uncentered JᵀJ without division by M; its ridge parameter therefore has different units. Both use a dense direct solve.

slides.title: Small-system SR comparison
slides.subtitle: 3×3 cylinder, RBM64; M=128, P=2989; one SGD step, η=0.001
slides.settings_note:
Ridge: τ = 0.001
MinSR: relative cutoff 10⁻¹², absolute cutoff 0
slides.footer: Same weights and 128 IID samples from current NQS probabilities. Energies evaluated over all 19,855 configurations (ED ground E/t = −4.385697). One batch and one step illustrate the methods, not convergence or superiority.

slides.title: Density on the lattice
slides.footer: Actual 4×4 cylinder DMRG density, t=1, U=16.74, Nmax=4. Color scale resolves weak edge/bulk variation; values are mean occupations, not a single occupation configuration.

slides.title: Nearest-neighbor correlations
slides.footer: One-body coherence, not density-density correlation. Both endpoints lie in the strip; dashed links are periodic y bonds. Fixed N gives ⟨b_i⟩=0. Nonzero NN coherence alone does not establish superfluidity or criticality.

slides.title: VMC accuracy targets
slides.footer: Central strip = two middle x columns. Form composite observables before blocking. Point and precision criteria must both pass; a large error bar cannot earn a pass.

slides.title: Tighten Conv2D VMC
slides.footer: Same Conv32 architecture. Stage B: M=1024; C: M=2048 with decreasing learning rate and SR shift. Fresh walkers equilibrated for 4096 proposals. B uses seed321; C independent confirmation seed654.

slides.title: Correlations beyond NN
slides.footer: Raw directed anchor-line estimates with conditional SEM; diagonal excluded. Individual pairs are noisier than central NN averages. The 5% summary target does not apply to this whole curve.

slides.title: Configurations and budgets
slides.footer: Architecture-specific optimization budgets; this is an accuracy comparison, not an equal-compute ranking. Warm starts restore inference weights only; optimizers and walkers are fresh.

slides.title: Takeaways and next steps
lines: Conv2D and Transformer meet summary targets on both cylinders.
FC passes on 4×4; the wider 6×4 fit has a 2.22% energy gap.
RBM128 has a 1.51% gap on 4×4; 6×4 remains untested.
Basic Jastrow stays a physical baseline without further adaptation.
The matched MinSR test has no resolved winner; the small test is one step.
slides.footer: Finite cylinders at U/t=16.74 are a building benchmark. No thermodynamic limit, critical exponents, larger-system fidelity or universal architecture ranking is inferred.

slides.title: Ridge SR: definitions
slides.footer: M counts retained configurations, not independent samples. P counts trainable parameters. These formulas use the real, positive-amplitude ansatz and fixed-N sector.

slides.title: Imaginary time and the metric
lines: SR matches a linearized variational step to imaginary-time evolution.
slides.footer: First-order wavefunction and second-order distance expansion; Monte Carlo estimates replace expectations. S is the real quantum geometric metric, not the energy Hessian.

slides.title: Ridge SR as least squares
lines: The code assigns d as the gradient to native SGD.
slides.footer: The Euclidean parameter penalty stabilizes ill-conditioned directions and changes the step. No Adam is applied after SR; the learning-rate convention absorbs the energy-gradient factor of two.

slides.title: The exact sample-space solve
lines: Same full batch and ridge; use the smaller dense system.
slides.footer: For positive tau, this is the same regularized direction in exact arithmetic. Centered sample rank is at most min(P,M−1). No additional sample, parameter or rank truncation is introduced.

slides.title: What ridge does to each mode
lines: Small-curvature directions are smoothly damped, not estimated reliably by assumption.
slides.footer: The ridge trades step fidelity for stability. A small sampled linearized step does not guarantee a small nonlinear wavefunction change or successful optimization.

slides.title: Relation to published MinSR
lines: Our ridge uses 1/(λ+τ); the optional comparison uses the published soft filter.
slides.footer: Chen & Heyl, Nature Physics 20, 1476–1481 (2024), doi:10.1038/s41567-024-02566-1, Methods Eqs.20–23. Zero modes require explicit handling; actual SGD update is −ηd.

slides.title: Cost, storage and precision
rows: Model derivatives may originate in float32
slides.footer: Costs exclude sampling and neural differentiation. Linear in P only at fixed M in the sample-space branch. Same-batch CPU audit: P=3681, M=256, primal/dual relative direction error 1.5×10⁻¹¹; not a long-run convergence proof.

slides.title: Comparison with the 1D routine
lines: $\tau=\lambda_{\rm sum}/M\quad\text{matches ridge units; centering still differs.}$
1D CPU code solves in float64; 2D solves on the training device in float64.
slides.footer: Changes to centering, ridge units and device are separate from Jacobian vectorization. The user accepted the 2D formulation. Gauge shifts can affect parameter differences without changing normalized-state tangents.

slides.title: Observable estimators in VMC
lines: R is zero unless n_i > 0 and n_j < Nmax (row-action estimator).
Average sites/bonds within each sample, then apply time-block statistics.
slides.footer: The real positive-amplitude ratio preserves total particle number. For bond coherence average R_ij and R_ji; retain raw directed estimates separately. D_i is a factorial moment, not itself the number variance.

slides.title: Matched optimizer comparison
slides.footer: One optimizer seed; two evaluation seeds probe measurement variation, not independent training runs. Float64 Gram/solve/eigensolve; native SGD. Shared-GPU times are not isolated throughput benchmarks.

slides.title: First comparison: no clear winner
slides.footer: Both arms miss the energy target; central density and both NN directions pass. Paired conditional differences are unresolved (1.30 / 0.15 SEM). This short, single-training-seed test establishes no general advantage.
